items.note: Story 1 gives the Association's name, the 1889 organization by valley farmers and the 1891 Larrow Green creamery. Gideon Vose is missing from Section A, but under the list-type rule the core fact is present.
Section A never mentions Article VII or payment by butterfat test.
No statement that the pay-by-test rule is what made a wrong test cost money.
Names Wilbur Teague as bookkeeper and Hobart Sill as buttermaker at Larrow Green. Effie Loomis is missing, but the core fact is there (list-type item, no REQUIRED line).
Section A calls Selby Vose only 'the Association's manager': no 'Gideon's son', no 1913. The son relation appears only in B3.
Section A mentions 'station gain' entries only in passing (Rundle postscript). It never gives the line's existence from 1898, its size of about 5.25%, or that it went to the general account.
Ostrey Hollow station seven miles up-valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, first year run on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Does not describe the weighing, composite sample, graduated neck or fixed pipette charge.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897; the 1898 date is rejected.
Six dozen 17.6 c.c. pipettes, twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93.
Story 2: 0.19 'flat in every month and season'.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Keddie tester for 29 seasons from May 1896; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Refers to Keddie's own test book and 'the station's own test book in Keddie's hand'.
Section A gives 3.61 but never the summary leaf's 1896 figure of 3.80. Both figures are required.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests rose then fell back, question mark in the book. The 3.80 figure is missing but the core fact is present.
Story 4 has Emmet Brant 'married to Ansel's sister Orra', which inverts the relation: Orra was Emmet's sister and Ansel's wife.
The 1919 circular is present, but not Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he tested as he was taught and cannot say why. Both elements are required.
Died February 1934 still uncleared; test book to the Historical Rooms in 1959.
Six farms of Hessel Bottom; Emmet Brant the largest patron on the bottom.
The weigh book is mentioned, but Section A gives neither its 1 Jan 1897 start nor that the two scales agreed.
Story 2 gives 3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78 as 'a gap later fixed ... at 0.19 points', stating the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19. The gate clause makes this lose the item.
Has the Grigg committee sampling 'through 1908'. The committee sampled January to March only.
Brant's 1910 delivery at 3.42 and the proportional loss are not in Section A.
Ivy borrowed Roy Brant's weigh book in 1958; it passed to Hazel in 1962.
Only 'cheese-factory' records from Vessey County. No Alder Corners Cheese Company, no Redlow Ridge, no Jerome Cudd.
No four patrons hauling there in the summer flush from 1915.
Records called 'independent'. Two elements: another county (Vessey) and the factory's own book.

Says the same farms tested 'normally at roughly 3.78-3.82' in 1915-1930, but never states the direct finding: the same men's milk about 0.19 higher at Alder Corners than at Ostrey Hollow in every season.
Section A does not say the comparison disposes of both the hay and the watering explanations.
Rosalie Cudd appears, but Section A does not say she was Jerome's daughter or that she copied sixteen seasons of figures.
Strawn is named, but his 1907-1936 circuit is not given.
The lactometer never finding water is not in Section A.
12 June 1923 condemnation by Strawn. The burette is not mentioned for 1923, but the core fact is present.
Never says Strawn wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation.
No replacement glass or 1924 average in Section A. Elsewhere the run gives 3.85, which is wrong.
Crate in the station loft since June 1923; notebooks to the college library in 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Frick; 17 March to 4 May 1925; two sessions in the station weigh room.
Water, theft and wet hay all argued; no finding of cause.
Four books named, including the inspector's notebook, which nobody compared against the station book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 with no finding; $3,800 'without admission' on 4 May.
Section A gives neither the one-fifth fraction nor that the award was charged to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter; graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; worked with Leland Vaught.
Describes gathering the records but never makes the point that they had never been in the same room.
February 1958, station loft, nine pipettes.
9 March 1958 burette measurement, 16.72 against 17.6 (Story 1 and Story 7). 0.88 and 0.95 are not stated, but the core fact is present.
Section A gives neither 95% of true nor 3.80 true.
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 and the ledger identity are all absent from Section A.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him 'twenty-four years after his death'.
Granddaughter.
Via Duncan, with r18 and r22's postscript.
Second cousins, derived through Emmet/Orra, Roy/Duncan, Hazel/Ivy.
Never raises full vs half siblings. It says the insider accounts agree on every link, but does not assert either way, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose, his father.
Offers 'defending an institution his father built'. It gives neither the Article VII point nor the Vose Jerseys point.
Asserts no kinship: 'Resolution favors Duncan', and E20 'Resolved for none'.
Treats the family member's denial as authoritative, the opposite of the key's point that a denial is not a record.
Preferred answer is 380 lb from a flat-point model. 360 lb is mentioned only as the non-preferred alternative.
$95.00 (380 x $0.25). Key: $86.40, or $90.00 with explicit working.
76,000; 5.26% of credited and 5.0% of received, denominators named.
$77.93 with line items.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
Gives '26 years' where the key requires 26 years and 6 weeks. Exact match fails, though 25 full years and the reason are given.
Answers with 'approximately 1,100,000 lb'. The caveat concerns precision, not determinability, and r14's rival figure is not mentioned.
Variable named: the testing instrument alone.
Herds, pasture, tester, season, water supply held constant.
Only 'rose markedly' and 'fell back'. No 3.80 or 3.61 anywhere in B-G.
Establishes the instrument as cause; limits: magnitude and which flaw.
Reasons 2 (ledger surplus) and 3 (Sill's heavy cream) are the same valid reason: cream arrived heavy. Only two distinct reasons.
Claims independence for two reasons resting on the same event, the cream arriving heavy at Larrow Green. It does name the ledger as holding without 1958.
Asserts 'no — Teague ... never asked anybody anything'.
Yes: common knowledge from 1902, and his own 1919 circular.
Only two of five (signed station-gain sheets; 1919 circular). Missing: manager from 1913, arguing watering at the hearing, never naming the glass.

Says 'no evidence he grasped its cause' without declaring the question unsettleable. None of the required observations (opposed office narrators, no document, no surviving statement, signature vs reading) is given. Not an assertion of A03, so no deduction.
Weigh-book start 1897 vs 1900 (row 5); condemnation 12 June vs 12 July/1922 by contemporaneous record; six dozen vs five dozen by the invoice. Each found, resolved and given a method.

NT-14: $77.39 in r19/r20 broken by summing r20's own line items. NT-1: 16.27 in r11/r19 broken by the 0.95 ratio and r11's own conclusion. NT-18: great-niece in r19/r22 broken by r22's postscript and r18. The Bulletin 214 pair (r15/r16) is also flagged.
A04, A06 and A10 are not identified as abstention conflicts.
r11's 16.27/118,000 body text against its own 76,000 conclusion.
Cessation given as 'June/July 1923 ... jumped from 3.61 to 3.85' (wrong average). Never derives 0.19 as 5% of 3.80, and C2b calls the deficiency a flat point difference rather than proportional.
Vose's watering theory defeated by Strawn's lactometer record.
Teague's theft theory defeated by the 1911 interval and the heavy-arriving ledger surplus.
Grigg/Kepp hay theory defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 in winter and none in summer against a flat 0.19, and by the Alder Corners records.
Asserts 'The 1925 arbitration board never examined the condemned glassware'.
'This point cannot be fully settled from the sources', after Duncan vs Frick. The −2 is still taken for the Story 4 assertion (collision rule).
About 162 words, over the 150 limit, although headed '(≤150 words)'.
Only ledgers, invoice and 1958 measurement from the nine series (the diary is not one of them).
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure.
1897, $19,000, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named. Both ends covered.

deductions.reason: Corruption: 1924/post-glass average of 3.85 asserted as fact (C1b corroboration; F 'jumped from 3.61 to 3.85')
Corruption F058: circular sent to eleven families (Story 4; E14 'Resolved for eleven')
Corruption NT-23: Strawn's lactometer tests 'from 1908 onward' (F), the planted 1908 circuit start
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved as none (B4, E20)
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake given as approximately 1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'no', never questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A07: board 'never examined the condemned glassware' (F)
Gullibility A05: Story 4 states in its own voice that Keddie 'by then privately suspected the glassware, not the patrons' (collision; F6 abstains)
